content:
Thanks a lot for the kind words about the viewer!

Yes, I'm looking into it. Since you can control each of your fighter's 15 joints, the input describes both bodies in full: 19 points and 15 joints per fighter, which makes 68 of the 72 lines. I was so focused on the physics (balance, creating your own moves, lots of room for creativity) that I didn't think about the size of the input, and I had missed the stub best practices. 

When I saw 5DN1L's comment, my first reaction was: oops! 😅

I'm now looking into a lighter input, or maybe a change in the game mechanics.

The viewer is brilliant, but 72 lines of input seems a bit much to me. Not sure if it can be simplified, though :O
Upvoted for the work!

I haven't read the statement in detail or done any play-testing yet, but the official best practises state that:

> The number of variables per loop should not exceed 10.

https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/creating-your-own-puzzle

I'm not sure whether there's any bot game on CG that requires reading 72 lines of input per turn 😅
